newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein steady, tender cancelled.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein steady, tender cancelled.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were mostly steady in late trading on Tuesday, while a crude palm oil tender was cancelled because the top bid was below the seller's expectations, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,430-35 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening. A 500-tonne crude palm oil tender in the North Sumatran city of Medan was called off as the seller wanted 1,216 rupiah/kg against the top bid of 1,190. The previous tender price was 1,170 rupiah.
"The seller will re-tender on Friday," one trader said.
The traders said palm olein prices had increased from 1,420-25 rupiah/kg at Monday's close because of tight supply in the wake of active exports.
"Export prices are very good, and players are hiking their prices knowing very well that if they cannot sell in the local market they can always export," one trader said.
"But I think the real supply crunch will come towards the end of the month because exports have been very good."

Data from Belawan Port showed that the MT Theresa will leave for Pasir Gudang, Malaysia, with 5,600 tonnes of crude palm oil on Wednesday, while the MT Minosa will leave for China on Wednesday with 2,000 tonnes of palm olein.
The MT Istana-VI will arrive at Belawan on Wednesday with 4,800 tonnes of crude palm oil.
